theScopeQuestion:
SETTLED 2026-09-07. THE TOPIC SURVIVES, AND IT IS NOT ONLY AMERICAN SMOKEHOUSE.

THE WORRY WAS REASONABLE. The site already publishes best-korean-restaurants-london and best-turkish-restaurants-london, and Time Out's own caption for its barbecue guide reads 'from Texan style platters and Jamaican jerk to Korean and Japanese BBQ joints'. If Korean tabletop and Turkish ocakbasi were most of London barbecue, this guide would be a thin American remainder sitting on top of two existing pages.

THEY ARE NOT. EIGHT EDITORIAL LISTS WERE READ IN FULL AND COUNTED. Korean plus Turkish plus Japanese tabletop costs each list between one and three names:
  Time Out, ranked 12      - loses Kintan, Pochawa Grill, Kanpai Classic          -> 9 remain
  SquareMeal, 19           - loses Mangal II, Yanji                              -> 17 remain
  Secret London, 18        - loses Jin Go Gae, Gogi, Zuma                        -> 15 remain
  The Nudge, 16            - loses Chungdam, Olle, Kanpai Classic                -> 13 remain
  The Handbook, 15         - loses Olle Korean Barbecue                          -> 14 remain
  Hot Dinners, 15          - loses Mangal 2, Black Axe Mangal, Oklava            -> 12 remain
  The Standard, 14         - loses Mangal 2                                      -> 13 remain
  Eater London, 8          - loses Black Axe Mangal, FM Mangal                   -> 6 remain

SO THE REMAINDER IS 6 TO 17 VENUES PER LIST, WHICH IS A GUIDE. And the remainder is three distinct things, not one:
  1. AMERICAN SMOKEHOUSE - Smokestak, Texas Joe's, Big Easy, Bodean's, Red Dog Saloon, Burnt Smokehouse, From The Ashes, Black Cactus, Lil' Nashville, The Blues Kitchen, Prairie Fire.
  2. DIASPORA SMOKE, the most interesting part and the part no competitor has organised - a Texan smoker cooking somebody else's food. Cue Point (Afghan-Texan, and Time Out's number one), Hon's BBQ (Chinese-Texan, Hackney Wick), Maureen's Brixton Kitchen (Jamaican jerk), Smokey Jerkey.
  3. LIVE FIRE AND WOOD GRILL - Temper, Brat, Acme Fire Cult, Humo, Cinder, Firebird, Whole Beast, Kudu Grill, Parrillan, Coal Rooms, Ekstedt at the Yard.

IS LIVE FIRE THE SAME TOPIC AS BARBECUE? YES, AND THE PUBLISHERS DECIDED IT, NOT US. Eater's page carries the h1 'Here Are London's Best Live Fire Restaurants' and the title tag 'The Best Barbecue Restaurants and Live Fire Cooking in London' - one page, both words. SquareMeal opens its BBQ list with Firebird and includes Parrillan, Smoking Goat, Kolae and AGORA. The Standard's barbecue list includes Brat, Humo and Brigadiers. Time Out ranks Acme Fire Cult eighth of twelve. Temper appears on FOUR of the eight lists. Five publications independently put live-fire grills inside their barbecue guides, so a guide that excluded them would be narrower than every source it was built from.

BUT THE READER WHO SEARCHED FOR BRISKET DID NOT COME FOR A GALICIAN CHOP. That tension is real, and it is what the facetAxis below exists to resolve: one page, split by heat source and time, so somebody who wants a smoker is never sent to an asador by accident. That split is the single most useful thing this guide can do and not one of the eight sources does it.

WHAT TO DO ABOUT KOREAN AND TURKISH. Do not collect them and do not publish them here. Every source will hand them to the extractor anyway, so drop them at recording and say why in the corpus note. In the article, one line pointing at /best-korean-restaurants-london/ and /best-turkish-restaurants-london/ does the reader more good than a token entry each - and per trap 7, any count those venues carry belongs to those topics, never to this page.
theBrisketFinding:
THE DISH-LEVEL SEARCH HAS NO INDEPENDENT COVERAGE AT ALL, AND THAT IS THIS TOPIC'S REAL PROBLEM.

`best brisket london`, run 2026-09-07, returned ten results. Here is every one of them:
  RestaurantGuru x2      aggregator, scraped review counts
  Tripadvisor x2         aggregator, one of them a single user review
  Yelp                   aggregator
  bigeasy.co.uk          THE VENUE'S OWN SITE, titled 'Why We Serve the Best Beef Brisket in London'
  themeatery.co.uk x2    THE VENUE'S OWN SITE, one page titled 'Where Can You Find the Best Brisket in London?'
  smokestak.co.uk        THE VENUE'S OWN SITE
  timeout.com            the general BBQ list, the only editorial result and not about brisket

ZERO independent editorial. Every answer a reader gets to the most specific question in this topic is either a scraped aggregator or a restaurant selling itself - two restaurants have written SEO pages answering 'where is the best brisket in London' with 'here'. That is tier F wearing a guide's clothes, and it is ranking because nobody else has written the page.

TWO CONSEQUENCES.
  1. IT IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE GUIDE. This is the clearest opening any topic on this site has had: the query exists, the demand exists, and the answer currently comes from the restaurants themselves.
  2. IT IS A COLLECTION HAZARD. Those venue pages will surface on every dish-level search run during collection, they read like guides, and they must never be recorded. Tier F, weight 0, excluded at collection. themeatery.co.uk is the sharpest case: a restaurant running a page whose title is a reader's question.

RUN THE DISH-LEVEL QUERIES ANYWAY at collection - beef rib, burnt ends, pulled pork, jerk - but expect them to return venues rather than sources, and use them to find NAMES, not to find opinions.
theCountingProblem:
FOUR WAYS THIS CORPUS GOES WRONG. All four were seen on 2026-09-07.

1. STALE LISTS CARRYING DEAD RESTAURANTS. This topic churns harder than any other on the site. Secret London (April 2024) still names PITT CUE and HOTBOX; Culture Calling (August 2023) names HOTBOX and SMOKEHOUSE ISLINGTON; The Rare Welsh Bit names HotBox. All three are believed long closed. Eater's live fire map is dated 2022 and Hot Dinners' is July 2022. CHECK EVERY VENUE IS TRADING BEFORE RECORDING IT - and note that a source is not disqualified by carrying one dead venue, it is just old.

2. HEADLINE COUNTS THAT DO NOT MATCH THE PAGE. Culture Calling is titled 'Top 10: American Smokehouse Restaurants in London', its meta description says '5 All-American Smokehouses', and it names NINE. DesignMyNight's 'Top 10 Smokehouses in London' names SEVEN. Do not trust a headline number; count the page (halal.json hit the same thing on a '20 Affordable' list carrying 38).

3. DESIGNMYNIGHT'S BBQ PAGE IS MOSTLY PUBS RUNNING BARBECUE EVENTS. Read 2026-03-26, 16 names, and more than half are pubs and bars with a summer grill: Britannia - Smok'd, The Engineer, Pacific Tavern, THE ALCHEMIST LONDON - MONUMENT, World's End, The Lord Wargrave, The Star by Hackney Downs, Camden BBQ. The page title says 'BBQ Restaurants AND EVENTS' and the events are the majority. Recording it whole puts a cocktail chain into a barbecue guide. Scope it to the actual barbecue restaurants (Blues Kitchen Brixton, Dom Carnivoro, Cabana Brasil, Red Dog Saloon Shoreditch, Bodeans Camden, Sagardi, Smokestak, Acme Fire Cult) or leave it out.

4. TRAP 13 - VENUES ALREADY IN OTHER CORPORA. Checked 2026-09-07, and NO SOURCE URL in data/serp/barbecue.txt appears in any existing consensus file, so seeding is safe. The VENUE overlap is real but small, which is itself a finding: the American smokehouse end of London is almost entirely unrecorded on this site.

NOT ONE of Bodean's, Red Dog Saloon, Prairie Fire, Texas Joe's, Big Easy, From The Ashes, Black Cactus, Lil' Nashville, Cinder, Firebird, Goldies or Humo appears in ANY existing corpus. Roughly two thirds of this topic is new to the site.
TRAP 7 IS THE LIVE RISK: Smokestak, Temper, Brat and Acme Fire Cult all carry counts elsewhere. Rebuild against topics.includes('barbecue') only and never reprint a steak or Shoreditch count here.

GREP FALSE POSITIVES, ignore them: 'Brix' matches the word Brixton across nine corpora; 'Olle' in fish-and-chips.json is a substring, not the Korean barbecue restaurant; 'Temper' matches ordinary words. Confirm before merging anything on a substring hit.
awardBodiesChecked: BRITISH BBQ SOCIETY (bbbqs.com) - RESOLVED 2026-09-07, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. It is real, it is the body the brief named, and it is not tier A for this guide. Set up in 2008 by Toby Shea, it self-describes as 'the primary barbecue forum in the UK' covering 'all aspects of barbecue, from grilling to low and slow, competitions to classes', and its own YouTube channel calls it 'The Only Barbecue Competition Circuit in the UK'. THE COMPETITIONS JUDGE COOK TEAMS AT EVENTS, NOT RESTAURANTS. There is no published, dated results page naming restaurant winners anywhere on the site - the front end is a phpBB forum and a Facebook group. Do not record it as an award. It may still be useful as a COMMUNITY source if tier E is ever unblocked, since its forum is where UK pitmasters actually argue; treat that as tier E, not tier A.

GRILLSTOCK - DEAD, AND HAS BEEN FOR EIGHT YEARS. Confirmed 2026-09-07. The Bristol barbecue festival and smokehouse chain went into administration in 2017, closed its LONDON restaurant in December 2017, briefly emerged, then ceased trading entirely in October 2018 and was liquidated with all 23 staff made redundant (thecaterer.com, restaurantonline.co.uk). The festival was cancelled in 2018. Its competition was a team cook-off in any case. Not an award, not a source, not a gap - just gone. Recorded here so nobody checks it again.

MICHELIN - THE ONLY JUDGED, DATED, VENUE-LEVEL RECOGNITION IN THIS TOPIC, AND IT IS ONE VENUE. SMOKESTAK HOLDS A BIB GOURMAND IN THE 2026 MICHELIN GUIDE UNITED KINGDOM, confirmed 2026-09-07. That is judged, dated and about a venue, so it is worth carrying - but it is a value-for-money distinction, not a barbecue award, and it does not make Michelin an award body for this topic. guide.michelin.com is on the permanent403 list in data/sources.json; the readable routes are thenudge.com/bib-gourmands-in-london/ (ALREADY RECORDED in general.json, where Smokestak's Bib is already logged) and the Wikipedia substitute registered in sources.json. Per trap 2, file the Bib under Michelin and do not also count The Nudge's Bib page as an independent opinion.
NATIONAL RESTAURANT AWARDS - judged and dated but UK-wide and general, with no barbecue category. Trap 12 applies if anyone reaches for it. Not tier A for this topic.

ESTRELLA DAMM TOP 50 GASTROPUBS - checked for relevance and there is none. It ranks gastropubs; the pub-garden barbecue venues in DesignMyNight's list are not on it, and the topic's actual venues are not gastropubs. Do not record it.
NO JUDGED BRITISH BARBECUE RESTAURANT AWARD EXISTS. That is the conclusion after checking all four above. Under SKILL.md this sets the social floor at THREE independent voices, not two.

assessedAndExcluded.verdict: EXCLUDE. TESTED AND FAILED 2026-09-07, and it is the clearest content farm found on any SERP for this topic. Page assessed: /best-smokehouses-london/, 'Top 5 smokin' BBQ joints in London that bring the sizzle', 25 February 2025, byline Therun Nakkeeran.
assessedAndExcluded.finding:
IT IS A GENERIC 'FIVE BEST X IN LONDON' FACTORY. Its own related-posts rail carries '5 Best Tax Consultants in London for Smarter Financial Decisions', '5 Best Furniture Delivery Services in London Worth Booking for Easy Transport', '5 Best Yoga Classes in London', 'The best bird pet shop in London' and 'Best fish pet shops in London'. A site ranking tax consultants, furniture couriers and aquarium suppliers has not eaten the brisket. It carries an Affiliate Disclaimer and a boilerplate 'How we chose' block with no named criteria.

SECOND TELL, AND THE MORE USEFUL ONE: its five names - Salt's Smokehouse, Holy Smokes BBQ London, Smoke Daddies, Smokin' Aces - are largely mobile caterers and event-hire units rather than restaurants a reader can walk into. Not one of them appears on any of the eight editorial lists. That is what a keyword-matched list looks like when nobody visited.

theSourceMixVerdict:
ASKED AND ANSWERED 2026-09-07: NO, THE FLOOR IS NOT REACHABLE IN THIS ENVIRONMENT. But this topic fails differently from halal, and the difference matters.

THE FLOOR: no judged barbecue award exists (see awardBodiesChecked), so SKILL.md requires THREE independent social voices.

WHAT THIS PASS CAN DELIVER: 14 sources across 14 distinct domains. SIX tier B - Time Out, SquareMeal, The Standard, The Handbook, Eater London, DesignMyNight. EIGHT tier C - The Nudge, Secret London, Hot Dinners, The Picky Glutton, The Rare Welsh Bit, Destined for London, Time Well Spent, Culture Calling. ZERO tier A. ZERO tier D. ZERO tier E. Social voices available: 0 of 3.

HOW THIS DIFFERS FROM HALAL, WHICH WAS 7 OF 8 TIER C. The published tiers here are HEALTHY - six real mastheads with named editors, one of them ranked, and a genuinely rigorous multi-visit reviewer in The Picky Glutton. Nobody should look at this corpus and call it thin. THE FAILURE MODE IS THE BREAKFAST ONE INSTEAD: six mastheads agreeing with each other. Smokestak appears on ALL EIGHT lists read. Acme Fire Cult on six. Cue Point, Big Easy, Temper, Parrillan and Smoking Goat on four or more. Strip the top ten and the lists start diverging, which is exactly where the interesting venues are and exactly where the mastheads stop looking.

EXACTLY WHAT IS MISSING, AND WHAT WOULD FIX IT:
  1. TIER D (video) - blocked because APIFY_TOKEN is not set. CONFIRMED UNSET 2026-09-07: the variable is empty in the shell and there is no .env, only .env.example and .env.local. Setting it unblocks this immediately and it is the cheapest large win available. Barbecue is heavily filmed - an ordinary web search for Hon's BBQ surfaced a TikTok review (@kristabelplummer) without anyone looking for one - and the video tier is where the market stalls, residencies and brewery-yard pop-ups live. It alone would take the topic from 0 of 3 to 2 or 3 of 3.
  2. TIER E (community) - Reddit is blocked to curl AND to the browser pane here. NOT fixable from this environment. Only route is Rob pasting thread URLs by hand, which SKILL.md explicitly provides for. NOTE ONE ALTERNATIVE: the British BBQ Society runs a public phpBB forum at bbbqs.com/Forum which is not Reddit and is not blocked. It is a UK pitmaster community rather than a London diners' one, so it will over-index on home cooking and competition, but it is a genuine tier E candidate nobody has tried.
  3. TIER A - genuinely does not exist for barbecue. Smokestak's 2026 Michelin Bib Gourmand is the only judged, dated, venue-level recognition in the topic and it is one venue and not a barbecue award. Nothing to fix.

RECOMMENDATION: set APIFY_TOKEN and run the video tier BEFORE collecting, not after. Otherwise ask Rob before proceeding - per ask-dont-publish-gaps, the gap goes to him, never onto the page.

facetAxis.note:
THE AXIS IS HEAT SOURCE AND TIME - a smoker versus a grill - AND IT IS THE ONE THING EVERY SOURCE BLURS AND NO COMPETITOR PRINTS.

WHY NOT REGIONAL AMERICAN STYLE. Texas versus Kansas City versus Carolina whole-hog is how American barbecue guides are organised, and it does not survive contact with London. Across eight lists and roughly 45 distinct venues, ONE reads as Kansas City, NONE does Carolina whole-hog, and the Texas claim is made by three or four places. A five-value regional axis would leave three sections with one venue each. Texas is real enough to name inside an entry - Texas Joe's smokes over oak for up to 16 hours, Red Dog Saloon over hickory for 18 - but it is not how a London reader browses, because London has not got enough of each to choose between.

WHY NOT SMOKEHOUSE VERSUS LIVE FIRE AS A TWO-WAY SPLIT. It is the right primary cut but it is too coarse on its own: it puts a Bermondsey pit counter and a Mayfair tasting room in one bucket and a Catalan asador and an Afghan-Texan pop-up in the other.

SO: FIVE VALUES, ordered from longest cook to shortest. The first three are smoke, the last two are fire. A reader who came for brisket never has to read past value three, and a reader who came for a chop over embers can skip to five - which is precisely what the eight sources make impossible today.

VALIDATED AGAINST THE SOURCES: SquareMeal's 19 splits 8 smoke / 11 fire, The Standard's 14 splits 6 / 8, Time Out's ranked 12 splits 8 / 4 with the smoke at the top. Every list contains both and not one of them says so.

OUT OF SCOPE, AND SAY SO ONCE IN THE ARTICLE RATHER THAN CARRYING TOKEN ENTRIES: Korean tabletop grilling (/best-korean-restaurants-london/) and Turkish ocakbasi (/best-turkish-restaurants-london/). Japanese yakiniku and robata go with them - Kintan, Kanpai Classic and Zuma are already in japanese.json. Every source will hand these to the extractor; drop them at recording, not at writing.

values.label: Texas-style pit
values.describeAs: beef brisket and short rib left over oak or hickory for twelve to eighteen hours, sold by the slice with white bread and pickles

values.label: The American barbecue room
values.describeAs: ribs, wings, pulled pork and a bucket of sides, in a big loud room built for a table of six

values.label: Smoke from somewhere else
values.describeAs: the same low-and-slow smoker, cooking Afghan, Chinese or Jamaican food - a wagyu brisket rubbed with Afghan spice, or short ribs done Sichuan

values.label: Live fire and wood grill
values.describeAs: whole cuts and whole vegetables cooked fast over burning wood, where the fire is in the dining room and you can see it

values.label: Asador and parrilla
values.describeAs: the Iberian and South American grill - meat over embers on an adjustable rack, cooked to order rather than smoked ahead

facetAxis.considerAdding: JERK, if collection turns up enough of it. Maureen's Brixton Kitchen is fourth on Time Out's ranked twelve and Smokey Jerkey is on Eater's map, and Time Out ran a separate expert guide by the food writer Melissa Thompson leading on 'jerk chicken in Brixton'. Jerk is barbecue by any definition - pimento wood, a covered drum, hours - and it currently has no home in the five values above except as diaspora-smoke, which undersells it. If three or more jerk venues clear two sources, split it out; if not, leave it inside diaspora-smoke and say what it is in the entry.

formatSection.title: The smoker is in a brewery yard
formatSection.note:
THE SECTION NOBODY ELSE PRINTS, AND IT IS VERIFIED. A large share of the best-reviewed barbecue in London is not in a restaurant. It is in a brewery yard, a railway arch, a converted car park or a pub garden - which changes the hours, the weather risk, the booking and the queue, and none of the eight sources tells the reader that.

EVERY VENUE BELOW WAS CONFIRMED 2026-09-07, each against a source that is not the venue's own marketing:
  ACME FIRE CULT, Dalston - at 40FT Brewery, in a converted car park known as The Bootstrap off Dalston's main drag, sharing the site with Dusty Knuckle Bakery. A custom-built grill and smoker stand in the covered yard; 50 covers inside, 60 outside on a covered and heated terrace. A collaboration with 40FT's founder Steve Ryan. (Great British Chefs; The Staff Canteen; The Live Review)
  FROM THE ASHES, Hackney - 'Smokehouse focused on sustainable whole animal British produce. Based in Five Points Brewery, Hackney.' (the venue's own words, so use it for the fact and not as a source)
  HON'S BBQ, Hackney Wick - Unit 7, Queen's Yard, in The White Building, canal-side above Crate Brewery, on the former Silo site. 80 covers. Opened July 2026. (Hot Dinners; Restaurant Online)
  BLACK CACTUS, Walthamstow - trades at Burnt Faith Brandy House. Time Out lists it as 'Black Cactus at Burnt Faith Brandy House', seventh of twelve.
  CUE POINT, Kensington - Time Out's number one for 2026, cooking in Garden Bar & Grill's BEER GARDEN.
  BURNT SMOKEHOUSE, Leyton - 'the barbecue restaurant in a Leyton railway arch' (The Picky Glutton's own headline, already recorded in general.json).
  FIVE POINTS BREWING TAPROOM & COURTYARD - listed as a barbecue destination in its own right by The Nudge.
That is seven, and the pattern holds across the corpus rather than being three coincidences. Two of the eight lists are themselves organised around it: DesignMyNight's page is half pub-garden barbecue, and From The Ashes runs 'East London smokehouse sessions' in the Five Points courtyard with Acme Fire Cult, Uncle Hon's and Cue Point on the pits - four of London's best smokehouses cooking in one brewery yard on one day.

WHAT THE SECTION MUST CARRY PER VENUE: whose building it is, whether the seating is outdoors, and whose hours apply - the kitchen's or the taproom's. Per the house rule, the callout carries the one thing that ruins a trip, not an opening-times table.

TWO CANDIDATES WERE TESTED AND REJECTED, recorded so nobody re-runs them:
  SELLS OUT AND CLOSES - the brief's first suggestion and it is the right idea, but IT COULD NOT BE VERIFIED FROM THIS ENVIRONMENT. Targeted searches for sell-out language across London smokehouses returned nothing, and the only 'Sold out' text found on a venue site was From The Ashes' online pre-order shop, which is a courier product and not the dining room. It may well be true - it is true of the form generally - but printing it unverified would be inventing a fact that costs a reader a wasted journey. If somebody can confirm it venue by venue, it is a better section than this one. ASK rather than publishing it.
  MEAT BY WEIGHT - also unverifiable here. Texas Joe's is the obvious test case and texasjoes.co.uk does not resolve from this environment (curl returns 000 on three variants). WARNING: texasjoes.com DOES resolve and is A DIFFERENT BUSINESS - 'The Original Real American Smokehouse in the Philippines'. Do not use it for the London venue's menu, prices or booking link.

knownGaps: NO JUDGED BRITISH BARBECUE RESTAURANT AWARD EXISTS. Resolved 2026-09-07 against all three candidates the brief named. British BBQ Society judges cook teams at competitions, not restaurants, and publishes no dated restaurant results. Grillstock ceased trading in October 2018 and was liquidated. Michelin gives Smokestak a 2026 Bib Gourmand, which is judged, dated and venue-level but is one venue and is not a barbecue award. Tier A is empty and cannot be filled. See awardBodiesChecked for the full working.

TIER D (video) needs APIFY_TOKEN, CONFIRMED NOT SET 2026-09-07. This is the one blocker that is trivially fixable and it should be fixed before collection, not after. Barbecue is one of the most heavily filmed food subjects in London and the video tier is where the market stalls and brewery-yard residencies live - exactly the venues the six mastheads do not reach.

TIER E (community) CANNOT be collected here - Reddit is blocked to curl and to the browser pane. Only fix is Rob pasting thread URLs by hand. ONE UNTRIED ALTERNATIVE worth a look: bbbqs.com/Forum, the British BBQ Society's public phpBB forum, is not Reddit and is not blocked. It skews to home cooks and competition teams rather than London diners, so weigh it accordingly, but it is a real tier E candidate.

SMOKESTAK APPEARS ON ALL EIGHT LISTS READ, and Acme Fire Cult on six. The mastheads agree with each other about the top ten and diverge below it. That is the breakfast failure shape and no script checks for it - audit-source-mix.mjs flags a corpus over 70% social, not one that is six mastheads deep.

FOUR OF THE FOURTEEN SOURCES ARE MORE THAN TWO YEARS OLD - Eater (2022-23), Hot Dinners (July 2022), Culture Calling (August 2023), Secret London (April 2024) - and three of them name venues believed closed (Pitt Cue, HotBox, Smokehouse Islington). This topic churns faster than the site's others. Every venue needs a trading check before recording, not just before publishing.

THE `best brisket london` SERP RETURNS ZERO INDEPENDENT EDITORIAL - ten results, all aggregators or venue-owned pages. See theBrisketFinding. That is an opportunity for the guide and a hazard for collection, and it means dish-level searches will find names but not opinions.

THREE NEW DOMAINS NEED REGISTERING in data/sources.json before seeding: standard.co.uk (tier B), therarewelshbit.com (tier C), destinedforlondon.com (tier C, flagged). Two need adding to the excluded list: wunderlustlondon.co.uk and restaurantguru.com, plus tripadvisor.co.uk which is absent while tripadvisor.com is present. Smokehouse Islington is believed closed and there is also Chiswick Smokehouse (DesignMyNight) and Burnt Smokehouse (Leyton). DO NOT MERGE ON THE WORD. CUE POINT IS NAMED AT THREE DIFFERENT ADDRESSES ACROSS SOURCES and this is the single biggest identity question in the topic, because it is Time Out's NUMBER ONE. Time Out's news piece places it in Garden Bar & Grill's beer garden in KENSINGTON; SquareMeal says NOTTING HILL; another list says Ely's Yard, SPITALFIELDS. Separately, new-openings.json ALREADY CARRIES 'Garden Bar Grill & Smokehouse By Cue Point' as its own name (trap 17 - sources name either the host or the residency), and From The Ashes' event listing calls the same operation 'Cue-Point' with a hyphen (trap 4). HON'S BBQ appears as 'Hon's BBQ', 'Hon\u2019s BBQ' with a curly apostrophe, 'Hons BBQ' and 'Uncle Hon's'. Trap 9 (decode entities before norm() sees them) and trap 4 (check name-aliases first). It is ALREADY RECORDED in new-openings.json under five source records and in general.json, so trap 7 applies too - never print its new-openings count here. Confirmed address: Unit 7, Queen's Yard, The White Building, Hackney Wick E9 5EN.

TEMPER, BIG EASY, RED DOG SALOON, BODEAN'S AND THE BLUES KITCHEN ARE ALL MULTI-BRANCH, and the sources split between brand and branch: 'Temper' versus 'Temper Soho', 'Big Easy' versus 'Big Easy Covent Garden' versus 'Big Easy Bar.B.Q & Crabshack', 'Red Dog Saloon' versus 'Red Dog Saloon Shoreditch', 'Bodean's BBQ' versus 'Bodeans Camden', 'The Blues Kitchen' versus 'Blues Kitchen Brixton' versus 'Blues Kitchen Camden'. Handle per chains.json. Note Red Dog Saloon also trades in Liverpool, Nottingham, Southampton and Brighton, so any UK-wide source naming it needs scoping (trap 12).

ACME FIRE CULT - casing varies ('ACME Fire Cult' in The Nudge and The Handbook, 'Acme Fire Cult' elsewhere) and it is ALREADY IN vegan.json. It also has a SEPARATE spin-off, ACME TACO, at 40FT Brewery WALTHAMSTOW, opened April 2026 - a different venue at a different address under the same owners. Do not let a source naming 'Acme' merge them.

BRAT versus 'BRAT CLIMPSONS ARCH' - The Standard names the Hackney sibling, Eater names the Shoreditch original, and steak.json, british.json, seafood.json and general.json all already carry 'Brat'. Two venues or one brand? Decide once and record it, and never print a steak count on this page (trap 7).

IS THE LIVE-FIRE END IN THIS GUIDE AT ALL AT VENUE LEVEL? theScopeQuestion says yes as a category, but the individual calls still need a human: BRIGADIERS (The Standard's only Indian entry, already in indian.json, a JKS Indian barbecue room), EKSTEDT AT THE YARD (Swedish fire cooking, in british.json, seafood.json and sunday-roast.json), HUMBLE CHICKEN (Japanese yakitori), KILN and SMOKING GOAT and KOLAE and KHAO BIRD (all Thai, all in thai.json), AGORA (Greek), SUCRE and CABANA BRASIL and DOM CARNIVORO (South American). Each is cooked over fire and each has a natural home elsewhere on the site. The default should be: include where a barbecue source named it, put it in the live-fire or asador facet, and never reprint its other topic's count.

GREP FALSE POSITIVES, do not act on them: 'Brix' matches the word Brixton in nine corpora; 'Olle' in fish-and-chips.json is a substring, not the Korean barbecue restaurant; 'Tongue & Brisket' in cheap-eats.json is a salt beef bar and is almost certainly not barbecue - check before recording it as one.
